name: Structural model: Parent, Adult, Child
oneLine: Parent, Adult and Child name where content comes from - copied from parents (Parent), built fresh in the here-and-now (Adult), or replayed from your own childhood (Child) - not how mature or childish it sounds.
whatYouDid: You had to resist reading Dev's crossed arms and clipped tone as just "being immature" and instead place it structurally: a childhood-style protest being replayed, not a character flaw.
confusion: People assume Child always means childish and Adult always means mature or grown-up-sounding; the tell is that "Adult" is about the timing of the response - here-and-now, using present resources - not its tone. A panicked, badly-reasoned reaction can still be genuine Adult if it's really about what's happening right now, and a calm, articulate statement can still be Child if it's a replay of something decided decades ago.

fromBook.quote: When I am behaving, thinking and feeling as I did when I was a child, I am said to be in my Child ego-state.

expand.definition: The structural model sorts personality content into three parts by origin: Parent (exteropsyche, copied from parent-figures), Adult (neopsyche, built fresh as a response to the here-and-now), and Child (archaeopsyche, replayed from one's own childhood).
expand.otherFraming: Freud's id/ego/superego cover similar ground but are purely theoretical and generalized; Berne's ego-states are judged from observable behaviour and point to specific, named people in your own history, not a universal psychic structure everyone shares identically.
expand.tryThisToday: Pick one strong reaction you have today and ask: is this really about right now, or is it dated - copied from someone, or replayed from some younger version of me?
